terms.definition: Any bar or splice located next to the splice in question.
Gross cross-sectional area of the concrete member.
how the ends of stirrups and ties are bent, hooked, or extended.
the angle through which a reinforcing bar, stirrup, tie, or hook is bent from its original straight direction.
Web width of the flexural member.
Depth of the flexural member
Width of the supporting member.
Determined by the formula s_o = 100 + (350 - h_x)/3 mm, where s_o is capped between 100 mm and 150 mm.
The surface-to-surface gap between two bars or between a splice and an adjacent bar.
The unobstructed vertical distance between the surfaces of bars in adjacent layers.
The unobstructed distance between the surfaces of adjacent parallel bars in the same layer.
The unobstructed length of the column between the faces of the supporting members.
Ties that form a completely closed loop around the main reinforcement bars in a column. Their ends are anchored with proper hooks so the tie fully encloses the bars.
The concrete region enclosed by the outermost transverse reinforcement of the column.
The cross-sectional dimension of the column in the direction being considered.
Vertical structural members primarily carrying axial load and moment.
the concrete enclosed within the hoops, into which the U-stirrup hooks must be anchored.
Lateral restraint provided to reinforcing bars or concrete to improve ductility and prevent buckling or splitting.
A condition where framing members surrounding the joint provide adequate lateral restraint, potentially reducing the need for hoop reinforcement.
The critical region at the column ends where hoops must be closely spaced. It must be at least the maximum of: the largest column cross-sectional dimension, 1/6 of the column clear height, or 450 mm.
cross ties placed one after another along the member length engaging the same longitudinal bar.
A lap splice where the two overlapping bars are touching each other.

Spiral-type reinforcement made from a continuous bar or wire wrapped repeatedly around the longitudinal reinforcement in a helical or spiral form. Instead of separate individual ties, the reinforcement is continuous along the height or length of the member.
a straight bar with hooks at each end used to close the U-stirrup and complete the hoop.
The effective depth of the beam, measured from the extreme compression fiber to the centroid of the longitudinal tension reinforcement.
Nominal diameter of the reinforcing bar.

terms.term: Depth of the shallowest framing member
terms.definition: The smallest cross-sectional depth among all beams or members framing into the joint, defining the zone within which the reduced transverse reinforcement applies.

terms.term: Diameter of the smallest longitudinal bar enclosed
terms.definition: The nominal diameter of the smallest longitudinal reinforcing bar surrounded by the stirrup.
The nominal diameter of the transverse reinforcing bar forming the stirrup.
The distance from the extreme compression fiber to the centroid of the tension reinforcement.
length of the bar beyond the bend point at the free end of the bar
Specified compressive strength of concrete.
The interface between the beam end and the supporting member (column or wall).
The surface of the column or wall at the beam end where the beam frames in.
The design axial load on a member after applying load factors.

A structural element that primarily resists loads by bending. In BNBC seismic provisions, when the code refers to flexural members, it is usually referring to beams or beam-like elements. Supporting member width - The width of the column or other support,
In general, reinforcement of a beam.
the condition where the section reaches its bending capacity, associated with inelastic response under lateral loads.
A column or other member in a special moment frame resisting earthquake forces.
Structural members forming part of a lateral force-resisting frame.
Specified yield strength of reinforcement.
The total thickness of the wall or slab.
A curved or bent portion at the end of a rebar.
the bend angle at the end of the U-stirrup, required to be not less than 135° for seismic detailing.
Closed ties or continuously wound ties enclosing the longitudinal reinforcement.
closed transverse reinforcement loops provided to confine concrete and restrain longitudinal bars in a frame member.
Lateral movement of the frame beyond the elastic range, typically under seismic loading.
lateral movements of the frame beyond the elastic range, occurring during seismic events.
The diameter measured on the inner curved surface of the bent bar.
The region where beams and columns intersect in a structural frame.
The minimum length measured from the joint face over which the tighter tie spacing s₀ must be maintained;
The length over which two bars overlap to transfer force.
A connection of two bars by overlapping them a specified length so that force is transferred between them.
Bars connected by overlapping within a lap splice.
The full span of the beam between the faces of the supporting members.
Reinforcing bars running along the length of the compression member.
The primary tension or compression steel bars running along the length of the beam that pass through or terminate at the joint.
Steel bars placed along the length of a structural member to resist bending and axial forces.
The largest centre-to-centre distance between laterally supported longitudinal bars, which must not exceed 350 mm.

terms.term: Maximum nominal size of coarse aggregate
terms.definition: the largest standard size of coarse aggregate particles that is permitted or intended to be used in a concrete mix.
The greatest allowable center-to-center distance between adjacent reinforcing bars.
The overall cross-sectional depth of the beam.
The full span of the beam between supporting joints.
The cross-sectional width of a framing beam or member measured perpendicular to the span direction.
The smallest permitted inside diameter of a bent reinforcing bar, measured on the inside curve of the bend.
The nominal or design flexural resistance at a given cross-section.
The flexural capacity of the beam cross-section when the top fiber is in tension (hogging condition).
Slabs that span primarily in one direction and are designed to carry loads in that direction.
Reinforcing bars running in the same direction placed in multiple horizontal layers.
The cross-sectional dimension measured perpendicular to the shortest dimension.
The flexural capacity of the beam cross-section when the bottom fiber is in tension (sagging condition).
The quotient of the shortest dimension divided by the perpendicular dimension.
The maximum allowable tie spacing within the length l₀
hooks with geometry meeting seismic detailing requirements.
The smaller of the two principal cross-sectional dimensions of the member.
The lesser of the two cross-sectional dimensions (width or depth) of the column frame member.
Special Moment Frame, a seismic-force-resisting structural system.
The center-to-center distance between successive transverse reinforcement sets within the joint.
The maximum allowable spacing of transverse reinforcement within length l_o, which is the smallest of: 1/4 of the minimum column dimension, 6 times the smallest longitudinal bar diameter, or s_o.
The spacing in the middle region of the column, which must not exceed twice the spacing inside the confinement zone (2 * S_o).
A moment-resisting frame designed to meet special seismic detailing requirements.
Continuously wound reinforcement in a helical form enclosing the longitudinal bars.
A reinforcing bar's end that is bent in a specified shape and length according to code requirements.
Transverse reinforcement bars placed perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the beam to resist shear and confine the core concrete.
Hooks formed on transverse reinforcement (stirrups and ties) used to confine longitudinal reinforcement.
small reinforcing bars used to confine and support the main steel bars in beams and columns.
open or closed transverse reinforcement with hooks meeting seismic detailing requirements, used where hoops are not required.
The nominal diameter of the transverse tie reinforcing bar.
The center-to-center distance between successive transverse tie bars along the column length.
Closed loop reinforcing ties placed within a beam-column joint to provide confinement and shear resistance.
Hoop or tie reinforcement placed within and through the joint region to laterally confine reinforcing bars.
Reinforced concrete slabs that carry loads and bend in both directions — along the length and the width of the slab.
a stirrup bent into a U-shape forming one piece of a two-piece hoop assembly.
